text.S1: Near a great forest dwelt a poor woodcutter with his wife and his two children. The boy was called Hansel and the girl Gretel.
text.T1: Kwakali sikugonka masamu wakali kukkala munsi munsi asaka pati amukaintu wakwe abana bobilo. Mwana musankwa wakali |Hansel mpoona musimbi wakali Gretel.
text.T2: Munsi munsi asaka mpati kwakali kukkala sikugonka masamu amukaintu wakwe abanabobilo. Mwana musankwa wakali Hansel mpoona musumbi wakali Gretel.

text.S1: He had little to bite and to break, and when great scarcity fell on the land, he could no longer procure daily bread. Now when he thought over this at night in his bed, and tossed about in his anxiety...
text.T1: Cakulya cakali kukatazya kujana, eelyo ciindi cinji caali kunga nzala yabbuba, taakali kukonzya kuula cakulya. Nakaali kuyeeya ceeci lyoonse masiku inga wakali kwiile kusalauka cakutakkalikila……
text.T2: Cakulya cakali kukatazya , eelyo ciindi cinji caali kunganzala yabbubba, taakali kukonzya kuula cakulya. Lino naakali kuyeeya ceeci lyoonse masiku inga wakali kwiile kusalauka cakutakkalikila……..

text.S1: He groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.T1: Wakali koombooka akuti kumwinakwe, “Ino ncinzibiya citibe kulindiswe? Ino bana aba bacaangu tulabasanina nzi kuti katutukwe cakulya swebo lwesu tobilo?”
text.T2: Wakali koomboka akuti kumukaintu wakwe, “Ino ncinzi biya citibe kulindiswe? Ino bana aaba bacaangu tulabasanina nzi kuti katutakwe cakulya swebo lwesu tobilo?”

text.S1: “I'll tell you what, husband,” answered the woman, “Early tomorrow morn- ing we will take the children out into the forest where it is the thickest. There we will light a fire for them, and give each of them one piece of bread, and then we will go to our work and leave them alone. They will not find the way home again, and we shall be rid of them.”
text.T1: “Leka ndikwaambile omulumi wangu,” wakataba mukaintu “mafumina juunza kambundu tuya kubatola bana musaka akati eeni alyo mpolijalide sokwe. Tukakutule mulilo mpoona aumwi tukamupe kankwa, tukabasiye balikke swebo tukaye kukubeleka. Tabakwe kuyoojoka alimwi, mbube kuyooba ngimagolelo abo kwamana.”
text.T2: “Leka ndikwaambile omulumi wangu,” wakavwiila mukaintu, “mafumina juunza kambundu tuya kubatola bana musaka akati eeni aalya mpolijalide sokwe. Tukakutule mulilo mpoona aumwi, tukamupe kankwa, tukabasiye balikke swebo tukaye kukubeleka. Tabakwe kuyoojoka alimwi, ngaatikabe magolelo aabo kwamana.

text.S1: “No, wife,” said the man, “I will not do that; how can I bear to leave my chil- dren alone in the forest?-the wild animals would soon come and tear them to pieces.”
text.T1: “Peepe, omwinangu”, wakaamba musankwa, “Ooko inga nsekuciti”, ino inga ndalimvwa buti kusiya bana bangu akati asaka balikke? – banyama balaboola ono ono akubazapaula mutubeela-beela.
text.T2: “Peepe omwinaangu,” wakaamba musankwa, “Ooko inga nsekuciti; ino inga ndalimvwa buti kusiya bana bangu akati asaka balikke? – banyama balaboola ono ono akubazapaula mutubeela-beela.

text.S1: “O, you fool!” said she, “Then we must all four die of hunger. You may as well plane the planks for our coffins,” and she left him no peace until he con- sented. “But I feel very sorry for the poor children all the same,” said the man.
text.T1: “Maawe, ociyanga yebo! Wakaamba mutumbu,” Nkabela toonse tone nkokuti atufwe biyo anzala. Cabota ubambile limwi amupulanga amabbokesi akukuzikkilwa,” mutumbu oyu taakwe naakamupa ciindi cakuliyeeya mulumi kusikila awalo wakautambula muyeeyo oyu. “Nokuba boobo, ndaliswiila buumba kubana aba beendoma,” musankwa wakaamba.
text.T2: “Maawee, ociyanga yebo!” wakaamba mutumbu, “Nkabela toonse tone nkokuti atufwe biyo nzala. Cabota ubambile limwi amapulanga aamabbokesi aakuzikkilwa,” mutumbu ooyu taakwe naakapa mulumi ciindi cakuliyeeya kusikila awalo wakautambula muzeezo ooyu. “Nokuba boobo ndaliswiilila buumba kubana aaba beendoma,” musankwa wakaamba.

text.S1: The two children had also not been able to sleep for hunger, and had heard what their stepmother had said to their father. Gretel wept bitter tears, and said to Hansel, “Now all is over for us.” “Hush Gretel,” said Hansel, “do not distress yourself, I will soon find a way to help us.”
text.T1: Abalo bana aba lwabo bobilo tiibaali kucikonzya akoona nkaambo kanzala, alimwi bakamwvwa banyina bamwi mbuli mbobakaambila bawisi. Gretel wakalila ceetezya amisozi kayuumbulika, elo wakaambila Hansel , “Pele langa swebo aya ngamamanino esu.” “Umuna Gretel, “ wakaamba Hansel,” “Utapengi mukwesu, ndilajana nzila ititugwasye swebo.”
text.T2: Abalo bana aaba lwabo bobilo tiibakali kucikonzya akoona nkaambo kanzala alimwi bakamvwa banyina mbobakaambila bawisi. Gretel wakalila ceetezya amisozi, mpoona wakaambila Hansel, “Pele langa swebo aaya ngamamanino eesu.” “Umuna Gretel,” wakaamba Hansel, “Utapengi mukwesu, ndilajana nzila ititugwasye swebo.”

text.S1: And when the old folks had fallen asleep, he got up, put on his little coat, opened the door below, and crept outside. The moon shone brightly, and the white pebbles which lay in front of the house glittered like real silver pennies.
text.T1: Ciindi bamacembele aba nibakoona, walo wakabuka akusama kabaki kakwe, wajula citendele mpocili ansi, akuzwida anze. Mwezi wakali kubala kabotu kabotu, mabwe akali kumbele anganda akali kunyengema mbuli mali ansiliva.
text.T2: Ciindi bamacembele aaba nobakoona, walo wakabuka akusama kabaki kakwe, wajula citendele mpocili ansi, akuzwida anze. Mwezi wakali kubala kabotu kabotu, amabwe aakali kumbele ang’anda akali kunyengema mbuli mali ansiliva.

text.S1: Hansel stooped and put as many of them in the little pocket of his coat as he could Possibly get in. Then he went back and said to Gretel, “Be comforted, dear little sister, and sleep-in peace, God will not forsake us,” and he lay down again in his bed.
text.T1: Hansel wakafulama akubweza mabwe aye kabikka munkono zyacibaki cakwe aakali kukonzya kwela kabotu-kabotu. Elyo wakajokela akwaambila Gretel kati, “Koliiba, omuce wangu alimwi biya koona muluumuno, Leza takwe kutulekelezya pe,” mpoona wakanjila mubulo bwakwe awalo woona alimwi.
text.T2: Hansel wakabweza mabwe akubika munkkomo zya cibaki cakwe aakali kukonzya kwela kabotu kabotu. Mpoona wakajokela akwambila Gretel kati, “Koliiba omuce wangu alimwi biya koona muluumuno. Leza takwe kutulekelezya pe,” mpoona wakanjila mubulo bwakwe awalo woona alimwi.

text.S1: When day dawned, but before the sun had risen, the woman came and awoke the two children, saying, “Get up, you sluggards! We are going into the forest to fetch wood.” She gave each a little piece of bread, and said, “There is something for your dinner, but do not eat it up before then, for you will get nothing else.”
text.T1: Nokwakabo kulubundu-bundu, pesi kalitaninga pasula zuba, mukaintu wakabusya bana bobilo boonse, kati, “Amubuke nozitolo nywebo! Tuya musokwe kukutebba nkuni.” Wakabapa aumwi kankwa kaniini akuti, nkocili cimwi cisusulo, pesi mutalyi ciindi kacitana sika, nkaambo taaku cimbi ncomuyiilye.
text.T2: Nokwakaba kulubundu-bundu, pesi kalitana pasula zuba, mukaintu wakabusya bana bonse bobilo kati, “Amubuke nozitolo nywebo! Tuya musokwe mukutwbba nkuni.” Wakabapa aumwi kankwa kaniini akuti, nkocili cisusulo, pesi mutalyi ciindi kacitana sika, nkaambo taaku cimbi ncomutiilye.

text.S1: Gretel took the bread under her apron, as Hansel had the stones in his pocket. Then they all set out together on the way to the forest. When they had walked a short time, Hansel stood still and peeped back at the house, and did so again and again.
text.T1: Gretel wakagusya kankwa kakwe kuzwa mucisani, kali walo Hansel wakabikkide mabwe munkomo. Boonse antonwe bakatalika kweenda kuya musaka. Nobakeenda kwakaindi kasyoonto, Hansel wakaima luzutu akulanga munsi kwakali ng’anda kaya bucita mbweena oobu ciindi aciindi.
text.T2: Gretel wakagusya kankwa kakwe kuzwa mucisani, kali walo Hansel wakabikkide mabwe mu nkomo yakwe. Boonse antoomwe bakatalika kweenda kuya musaka. Nobakeenda kwakaindi kasyoonto, Hansel wakaima luzutu akulanga munsi kwakali ng’anda kayabucita mbweena oobo ciindi aciindi.

text.S1: His father said, “Hansel, what are you looking at there and staying behind for Mind yourself, and do not forget how to use your legs.”
text.T1: Bausyi bakati, “Hansel, ino ulanga nzi ooko ancocaalila musule? Koide kulikwabilila, alimwi kozumanana kweenda.”
text.T2: Bausyi bakati, “Hansel, ino ulangalanga nzi ooko ancocaalila musule? Koide kulikwabilila, alimwi kozumanana kweenda.”

text.S1: “Ah, father,” said Hansel, “I am looking at my little white cat, which is sitting up on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me.” The wife said, “Fool, that is not your little cat, that is the morning sun which is shining on the chimneys.” Hansel, however, had not been looking back at the cat, but had been constantly throwing one of the white pebble stones out of his pocket on the road.
text.T1: “Hii, bataata,” wakavwiila Hansel,” Ndisondela kaaze wangu utuba, uukkede atala aciluli cang’anda, uyanda kuti tulayane andime.” Batumbu bakati, “Ocifubafuba teesyi kaaze wako ulya, ndizuba limweka ansonje.” Hansel, walo taakali akulanga mangoye pe, pele wakali kusowa-sowa tubwe tutuba kuzwa munkomo kulosyel mumugwagwa.
text.T2: “Hii bataata,” wakavwiila Hansel, “Ndisondela kaaze wangu uutuba, uukkede atala Aciluli cang’anda, uyanda kuti tulayane andime.” Batumbu bakati, “Ocifubafuba teesyi kaaze wako uulya ndizuba limweka ansonje.” Hansel pele taakali kulanga kaaze, pele wakali kusowa-sowa tubbwe tutuba kuzwa munkkomo kulosyela mumugwagwa.

text.S1: When they had reached the middle of the forest, the father said, “Now, chil- dren, pile up some wood, and I will light a fire that you may not be cold.” Hansel and Gretel gathered brushwood together, as high as a little hill.
text.T1: Nobakasika asaka mpolili akati mudili-dili muya musiya, bausyi bakati, “Lino, nobana, amulundike nkuni ndimukutwide mulilo kutegwa mutabi ampeyo,” Hanzele aGretel bakalundika nkuni, zyakali kulampa mbuli kaulu.
text.T2: Nobakasika asaka mpolilema muya musiya, bausyi bakati, “Lino, nobana, amulundike nkuni ndimukutwide mulilo kutegwa mutabi aampeyo .” Hansel aa Gratel bakalundika nkuni aantoomwe, zyakali kulampa mbuli kalundu.

text.S1: The brushwood was lighted, and when the flames were burning very high, the woman said, “Now, children, lay yourselves down by the fire and rest. We will go into the forest and cut some wood. When we have done, we will come back and fetch you away.”
text.T1: Nkuni zyakayasigwa, eelyo mulilo niwakayakisya mukaintu wakati, “Bana lino, amoone munsi-munsi amulilo mulyookezye. Swebo tulainka musaka tukagonke zimwi nkuni. Twamanizya, tulajoka tumulonde tweende.
text.T2: Inkuni zyakayasigwa, mpoona mulilo niwakayakisya mukaintu wakati, “Nobana lino, amoone munsi-munsi amulilo mulyookezye. Swebo tulainka musaka tukagonke zimwi nkuni. Twamanizya tulajoka tumulonde tweende.

text.S1: Hansel and Gretel sat by the fire, and when noon came, each ate a little piece of bread, and as they heard the strokes of the wood-axe they believed that their father was near. It was not, however, the axe, it was a branch which he had fastened to a withered tree which the wind was blowing backwards and forwards. And as they had been sitting such a long time, their eyes shut with fatigue, and they fell fast asleep. When at last they awoke, it was already dark night.
text.T1: Hanzele aGretel bakakkala munsi amulilo, mpoona nolyakaba syikati aumwi wakalya kankwa kakwe, eelyo nibakamvwa kukkasa kwakeembe bakayeeya kuti bausyi bakali mufwiifwi, pesi tiicakali boobu pe, tikaali keembe pe, wakali mutabi ngwaakaangilila kucisamu ciyumu muuwo ngocaali kutola ooku akooku. Nobakakkede kwaciindi cilamfu, meso abo akaambo kakukatala, akafunya mukukatala mpoona twakabatola twakatola mwaange bakoona. Nobakasinsimuka kumanino kwakali mumudima wamasiku.
text.T2: Hansel aa Gretel bakakkala munsi amulilo, mpoona nolyakaba syikati aumwi wakalya kankwa kakwe, eelyo nibakamvwa kukkasa kugonka kwakeembe bakayeeya kuti bausyi bakali mufwiifwi, pesi tiicakali boobu pe, tiikaali keembe pe, wakali mutabi ngobakaangilila kucisamu ciyumu muuwo ngowakali kucitola ooku akooku. Nobakakkede kwa ciindi cilamfu, meso aabo akaambo kakukatala akafunya mukukatala mpoona twakabatola twakatola mwaange bakoona. Nobakasinsimuka kumamanino kwakali kale mudima wamasiku.

text.S1: Gretel began to cry and said, “How are we to get out of the forest now?” But Hansel comforted her and said, “Just wait a little, until the moon has risen, and then we will soon find the way.” And when the full moon had risen, Hansel took his little sister by the hand, and followed the pebbles which shone like newly-coined silver pieces, and showed them the way.
text.T1: Gretel wakatalika kulila kaamba kuti, “Ino lino tulazwa buti akati kasaka ano Hansel pele wakaumunzya muce wakwe akuti, “Kobatama biyo aniini, kusikila mwezi upole, calino lino tulaibona nzila. Mwezi nowakazwa woonse mujulu, Hansel wakajatilila mucizi wakwe kujanza, mbaabo bakatalika kucilila tubwe katuya kumweka mbuli nsiliva mpya bakaibona nzila baunka balobelela.
text.T2: Gretel wakatalika kulila kaamba kuti, “Ino lino tulazwa buti akati kasaka aano?” Hansel pele wakamumuzya musyoonto wakwe akuti, “Kobatama biyo aaniini, kusikila mweeezi upole, calino lino tulaibona nzila. Mwezi nowakazwa oonse mujulu, Hansel wakajatilila mucizi wakwe kujanza, mbaabo bakatalika kucilila tubbwe katuya kumweka mbuli nsiliva mpya bakaibona nzila baunka baloobelela.

text.S1: They walked the whole night long, and by break of day came once more to their father's house. They knocked at the door, and when the woman opened it and saw that it was Hansel and Gretel, she said, “You naughty children, why have you slept so long in the forest? We thought you were never coming back at all!”
text.T1: Bakeenda busiku boonse, kubucedo bakasiku amunzi waba wisi. Bakakonkomona kumulyango, mpoona mukaintu naakajalula akubona kuti mbaa Hansel aGretel, wakati, “Nywebo nobana batamvwi, ncinzi camupa koona ciindi coonse cilamfu boobu musokwe? Swebo twali kuti kwiina biya nomuya kujoka limbi!”.
text.T2: Bakeenda busiku boonse, kubucedo bakasika amunzi waba wisi. Bakakonkkomona kumulyango, mpoona mukaintu naakajula akubona kuti mbaa Hansel aa Gretel wakayi, “Nywebo nobana batamvwi, ncinzi camupa koona ciindi coonse cilamfu boobu musokwe? Swebo twali kuti kwiina biya nomuya kujoka limbi!”

text.S1: The father, however, rejoiced, for it had cut him to the heart to leave them behind alone. Not long afterwards, there was once more great scarcity in all parts, and the children heard their mother saying at night to their father, “Everything is eaten again, we have one half loaf left, and after that there is no more. The children must go. We will take them farther into the wood, so that they will not find their way out again; there is no other means of saving ourselves!”
text.T1: Nokwakaba boobu, bausyi, bakakondwa, nkaambo biya cakali bakopede kumoyo kusiya bana munsi balikke. Kakutana akwiinda ciindi nikwakamana waawa kwakaba nzala ilunda kasuko mumasena oonse, bana bakaswiilila banyina masiku kabaambila bansyi kuti; “Zyoonse biya zyamana kuligwa alimwi tujisi biyo cisela cacinkwa cacaala, kwamana waano nkokuti kwamwanina lyo. Aaba bana beelede kwiinka. Tulabatola kulamfu kwini musaka, kutegwa bataijani limwi nzila; kwiina biya imbi nzila mbotukonzya kupona swebo lwesu.”
text.T2: Nokwakaba boobu, bausi bakakondwa, nkaambo biya cakali bakopede kumoyo kusiya bana munsi balikke. Kakutana akwiinda ciindi nikwakamana waawa kwakaba nzala iilunda kasuko mumasena oonse, bana bakaswiilila banyina masiku kabaambila bausyi kuti; “Zyoonse biya zyamana kuligwa alimwi tujisi biyo cisela cacinkwa cacaala kwamana waano nkukuti kwamaaniina lyo. Aaba bana beelede kwiinka. Tulabatola kulamfu kwini musokwe kutegwa bataijani limwi nzila; kwiina biya imbi nzila mbotukonzya kupona swebo lwesu.

text.S1: The man's heart was heavy, and he thought, “It would be better for you to share the last mouthful with your children.” The woman, however, would listen to nothing that he had to say, but scolded and reproached him. He who says what must say what, likewise, and as he had yielded the first time, he had to do so a second time also.
text.T1: Ooyu mulombwana wakalimvwa kutyoka moyo, mpoona wakayeeya,” Ncibotu lyoonse kwaabana nokacaya abana bako.” Imukaintu nokuba boobu, kunyina ncaakali kuyanda kumuswiilla mutumi, wakali kwiile kumudyakaizya akumufubaazya. Ooyo weelede kwaamba nceelede kwaamba kacaamba, mbuli lyoonse, weelede biyo kuzumina alimwi alwabili.
text.T2: Ooyu mulombwana wakalimvwa kutyoka moyo, mpoona wakayeeya, “Ncibotu lyoonse kwaabana nokaceya abana bako.” Imukaintu nokuba boobu, kunyina ncaakali kuyanda kumuswiilila mulumi, wakali kwiile kumudyakaizya akumufubaizya. Ooyo weelede kwaamba ncaelede kwaamba kacaamba, mbuli lyoonse, weelede biyo kuzumina alimwi alwabili.

text.S1: The children were, however, still awake and had heard the conversation. When the old folks were asleep, Hansel again got up, and wanted to go out and pick up pebbles as he had done before, but the woman had locked the door, and Hansel could not get out. Nevertheless, he comforted his little sister, and said, “Do not cry, Gretel, go to sleep quietly, the good God will help us.”
text.T1: nokuba boobu ibana bakalicili kulanga nkabela bakamvwa cakali kwaambwa. Bapati nobakoona, Hansel alimwi wakabuka, kayanda kuzwida anze akubwezelela mabwe mbuli kusaanguna, pele mukaintu wakacikiya cijazyo, eelyo Hansel taakakonzya kuzwa anze. Nokuba boobo, wakakulwaizya muce wakwe, akuti,”Utalili,Gretel”
text.T2: Nokuba boobu, ibana bakacili kulanga, nkabela bakamvwa cakali kwaambwa. Ibapati nobakoona, Hansel alimwi wakabuka kayanda kuzwida anze akubwezelela mabwe mbuli kusaanguna, pele mukaintu wakacikkiya cijazyo, eelyo Hansel taakakonzya kuzwa anze. Nokuba boobo, wakakulwaizya muce wakwe, akuti, “Utalili Gretel!”

text.S1: Early in the morning came the woman, and took the children out of their beds. Their bit of bread was given to them, but it was still smaller than the time before. On the way into the forest Hansel crumbled in his pocket, and often stood still and threw a morsel on the ground. “Hansel, why do you stop and look round?” said the father, “go on.”
text.T1: Mbuli cilengwa kuseni-seni mukaintu wakabusya baana akubapa kusyonto kwacinkwa caka cede kuti balye aboobo cakulya caakali cisyonto kwiinda mazuba alyose.Mbuli nobakabweza lweendo lwakuya musyokwe Hansel wakaima cakutazunguna wakanjila munkomwe akusowa cakulya ansi”Hansel ,nciinzi ncolangaula ?”baka mubuzya bausyi.
text.T2: Mbuli cilengwa kuseni-seni mukaintu wakabusya bana akubapa kusyoonto kwacinkwa caka cede kuti balye aboobo cakulya cakali cisyoonto kwiinda mazuba olyonse. Mbuli mbobakabweza lweendo lwakuya musyokwe Hansel wakaima cakutazungaana wakanjila wakanjila munkomo akusowa cakulya aansi. “Hansel, ncizi ncolangaula?” bakamubuzya bausyi.

text.S1: “I am looking back at my little pigeon which is sitting on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me," answered Hansel.
text.T1: Ndiyandaula ka kwilimba ka kkele aciluli kayanda kundilaya”wakavwuwa Hansel.
text.T2: “Ndiyandaula ka kwilimba ka kkele aciluli kayanda kundilaya,” wakavwuwa Hansel.

text.S1: “Simpleton!” said the woman, “that is not your little pigeon, that is the morning sun that is shining on the chimney.” Hansel, however, little by little, threw all the crumbs on the path.
text.T1: ”Yebo Simpleton!ako takali ka kwilimba kako,ndizuba lyakuseni njobweni aciluli limunika’Cakuusa Hansel asyonto-syonto wakacisowa coonse cakulya ncakaji munkomwe lyakwe.
text.T2: “ Yebo Simpleton!” bakaamba bakaintu, “aako takali ka kwilimba kako ndizuba lyakuseeni ndyobene aciluli limunika”. Hansel, nokuba boobo, aasyoonto-syoonto, wakacisowa coonse cakulya ncaakajisi munkomo lyakwe.

text.S1: The woman led the children still deeper into the forest, where they had never in their lives been before. Then a great fire was again made, and the mother said, “Just sit there, you children, and when you are tired you may sleep a little; we are going into the forest to cut wood, and in the evening when we are done, we will come and fetch you away.”
text.T1: Aboobo lweedo lwamu syokwe lwaka zumanana bakeenda businzo bakasika akubu,sena nkobatanasikide.nobakeenda kasinzo kalanfu bakaima akukunka mulilo ,mpona bakati ku baana “kaamu lyokezya mwakatala mulale twagama mukutebba nkuni tuzomucinga masiku twapiluka.”
text.T2: Aboobo lwendo lwmusyokwe lwaka zumanana bakeenda musinzo bakasika akubusena nkobatanasikide. Nobakeenda kasinzo kalamfu bakaima akukunka mulilo, mpoona bakati kubana, “kumu lyookezya mwakatala mulale twagama mukutebba nkuni tuzoomucinga masiku twapiluka.”

text.S1: When it was noon, Gretel shared her piece of bread with Hansel, who had scattered his by the way. Then they fell asleep and evening came and went, but no one came to the poor children. They did not awake until it was dark night, and Hansel comforted his little sister and said, “Just wait, Gretel, until the moon rises, and then we shall see the crumbs of bread which I have strewn about, they will show us our way home again. “When the moon came they set out, but they found no crumbs...

text.S1: For the many thousands of birds which fly about in the woods and fields had picked them all up. Hansel said to Gretel, “We shall soon find the way,” but they did not find it. They walked the whole night and all the next day too from morning till evening, but they did not get out of the forest, and were very hungry, for they had nothing to eat but two or three berries, which grew on the ground. And as they were so weary that their legs would carry them no longer, they lay down beneath a tree and fell asleep.

text.S1: It was now three mornings since they had left their father's house. They began to walk again, but they always got deeper into the forest, and if help did not come soon, they would die of hunger and weariness. When it was midday, they saw a beautiful snow-white bird sitting on a bough, which sang so delightfully that they stood still and listened to it. And when it had finished its song, it spread its wings and flew away before them, and they followed it until they reached a little house, on the roof of which it alighted; and when they came quite up to the little house they saw that it was built of bread and covered with cakes, but that the windows were of clear sugar.

text.S1: Suddenly the door opened, and a very, very old woman, who supported herself on crutches,came creeping out. Hansel and Gretel were so terribly frightened that they let fall what they had in their hands. The old woman, however, nodded her head, and said, “Oh, you dear children, who has brought you here? Do come in, and stay with me. No harm shall happen to you.” She took them both by the hand, and led them into her little house. Then good food was set before them, milk and pancakes, with sugar, apples, and nuts. Afterwards two pretty little beds were covered with clean white linen, and Hansel and Gretel lay down in them, and thought they were in heaven.

Afterwards two pretty little beds were covered with clean white linen, and Hansel and Gretel lay down in them, and thought they were in heaven.

The old woman had only pretended to be so kind; she was in reality a wicked . When a child fell into her power, she killed it, cooked and ate it, and that was a feast day with her. Witches have red eyes, and cannot see far, but they have a keen scent like the beasts, and are aware when human beings draw near. When Hansel and Gretel came into her neigh- borhood,she laughed maliciously, and said mockingly, “I have them, they shall not escape me again!”

Early in the morning before the children were awake, she was already up, and when she saw both of them sleeping and looking so pretty, with their plump red cheeks, she muttered to herself, “That will be a dainty mouthful!” Then she seized Hansel with her shriveled hand, carried him into a little sta- ble, and shut him in with a grated door. He might scream as he liked, that was of no use. Then she went to Gretel, shook her till she awoke, and cried, “Get up, lazy thing, fetch some water, and cook something good for your brother, he is in the stable outside, and is to be made fat. When he is fat, I will eat him.”
Gretel began to weep bitterly, but it was all in vain; she was forced to do what the wicked witch ordered her.

And now the best food was cooked for poor Hansel, but Gretel got nothing but crab shells. Every morning the woman crept to the little stable, and cried, “Hansel, stretch out your finger that I may feel if you will soon be fat.” Hansel, however, stretched out a little bone to her, and the old woman, who had dim eyes, could not see it, and thought it was Hansel's finger, and was astonished that there was no way of fattening him.

When four weeks had gone by, and Hansel still stayed thin, she was seized with impatience and would not wait any longer. “Now, Gretel,” she cried to the girl, “be active, and bring some water.Let Hansel be fat or lean, tomorrow I will kill him, and cook him.”

text.S1: “Just keep your noise to yourself,” said the old woman, “all that won't help you at all.” Early in the morning, Gretel had to go out and hang up the cauldron with the water, and light the fire. “We will bake first,” said the old woman. “I have al- ready heated the oven, and kneaded the dough.” She pushed poor Gretel out to the oven, from which flames of fire were already darting. “Creep in,” said the witch, “and see if it is properly heated, so that we can shut the bread in.”And once Gretel was inside, she intended to shut the oven and let her bake in it, and then she would eat her,too.

text.S1: But Gretel saw what she had in her mind, and said, “l do not know how l am to do it; how do you get in?”

“Silly goose,” said the old woman, “The door is big enough; just look, I can get in myself!”and she crept up and thrust her head into the oven. Then Gretel gave her a push that drove her far into it, and shut the iron door, and fastened the bolt. Oh! then she began to howl quite terribly,but Gretel ran away,and the godless witch was miserably burnt to death.

text.S1: Gretel,however, ran like lightning to Hansel, opened his littlestable, and cried, “Hansel,we are saved! And as they had no longer any need to fear her, they went into the witch's house, and in every corner there stood chests full of pearls and jewels.

text.S1: The duck came to them, and Hansel seated himself on its back, and told his sister to sit by him. “No,” replied Gretel, “that will be too heavy for the little duck; she shall take us across, one after the other.” The good little duck did so, and when they were safely across and had walked for a short time, the forest seemed to be more and more familiar to them, and at length they saw from afar their father's house. Then they began to run, rushed into the parlor, and threw themselves into their father's arms. The man had not known one happy hour since he had left the children in the forest; the woman, however, was dead. Gretel emptied her pinafore until pearls and precious stones ran about the room, and Hansel threw one handful after another out of his pocket to add to them. Then all anxiety was at an end, and they lived together in perfect happiness. My tale is done, see the mouse run, whoever catches it, may make himself a big fur cap out of it.
text.T1: Mpona kadada kakabola ukubabweza,Hansel mpona wakatanta amusana wakadada ,wambila mucizi kuti atante awalo “peepe kadada kaceesya kalaminwa ,kalatutola omwe-omwe”wakavwuwa Gretel.kadada kakazuzikizya mbobakaamba.Nobakamana kuzubuka mulonga bakabweza lweendo lwakuya kumaanda bakaboona nzila itozya kung’anda yakalizibya ,nobakazumanana kweenda amunzi mpobali kukkala akali bonya,mpona bakazuza canguzu,bakanjila mung’anda akukumbata bausyi cakukkomana.Bakakkomana bauyi kaambo kuti bakali buumi bwakuusa kuzwa bana nobakasweka musyokwe,mukubula coolwe bakaintu bakafwa ciindi eco,Gretel wakaguusya mabwe akali munkomwe mwakwe a Hansel wacita mbubwena bakabika mabwe antomwe akuyowa mpokwamana ,Hansel a Gretel kusanganya abausyi bakazumanana kukkala cakukkomana mbulikwasyi.. mpokamina kaano;
text.T2: Mpoona kadada kakaboola, mpoona Hansel wakatanta amusana wakadada, akwaambila mucizi kuti atante awalo, “peepe kadada kaceyesya kalaminwa, kalatutola omwe-omwe,” wakavuwa Gretel kadada kakazuzikizya mbobakaamba. Nobakamana kuzabuka mulonga bakabweza lweendo lwakuya kumaanda bakabona nzila iitozya kung’anda yakalizibya nobakazumanana kweenda amunzi mpobaali kukkala akalibonya mpoona bakazuza canguzu bakanjila mung’anda akukumbata bausyi cakukkomana. Bakakkomana bausyi nkaambo kakuti bakali buumi bwakuusa kuzwa bana nobakasweeka musyokwe mukubula coolwe bakaintu bakafwa ciindi eeco, Gretel wakagusya mabwe aakali munkkomo yakwe a Hansel wakacita mbubwena bakabikka mabwe aantoomwe akuyoowa mpokwakamanina, Hansel a Gretel kusanganya abausyi bakazumanana kukkala cakukkomana mbuli mukwasyi. Mpokamanina kaano;
